A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIPR research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original phylogenetic inference experiments on DS1–DS11 and SARS-CoV-2 genomes, including likelihood estimates, posterior summaries, convergence traces, and timing measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those inference results and reports additional simulations, tree-space coverage measurements, dataset statistics, and computational scaling results.

M1.justification: The independent log-normal distance distributions, single-linkage tree construction, closed-form density, and LOOR, reparameterization, and VIMCO estimators remain unchanged. Algorithm input declarations and redistributed explanations clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: The original twelve genomic datasets are retained. Section 4.4 and Appendix B.3 add two synthetic evaluation regimes: neutral coalescent/infinite-sites MS datasets and Kingman/Jukes-Cantor datasets with known generating trees. This substantially extends evaluation beyond observed genomic data and their subsets.

E2.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a limited quantitative comparison with cubeVB's restricted tree-space coverage, previously discussed qualitatively. It does not add a fitted cubeVB likelihood benchmark. BEAST and VBPI10/VBPI20 remain in the existing comparisons; relocating VBPI20 table entries does not remove that comparator.

E3.justification: The runtime study replaces COVID-19 subsets containing 3–72 taxa with simulated datasets containing 8–512 taxa and 1,000 sites. It changes the stopping rule from 1,000 iterations to five minutes or 1,000 iterations, whichever occurs first. New protocols also specify MCC-based cube-space assessment and known-tree checks using ten eight-taxon simulations, 10,000 optimization iterations, and 10,000 posterior samples.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of posterior mass excluded by cube space, pairwise Hamming-distance characteristics, and recovery of known tree lengths and likelihoods. The revised scaling study also measures parameter counts. These investigate representation coverage, approximation failures, and computational bottlenecks beyond v1's posterior summaries and convergence plots.

E5.justification: Appendix B.4 newly identifies the parenthesized uncertainties as standard errors estimated using 100 bootstrap samples. The numerical uncertainties and existing chain/restart counts are retained, so this establishes improved reporting rather than additional experimental replications.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 1–2 are numerically preserved in v2 Tables 6–7, and all twelve appendix convergence traces are retained. Substantial new results include 15.2–99.9% of sampled trees lying outside the assessed cube space, parameter-count comparisons, and long-tree underestimation. The replacement runtime study reports approximately linear VIPR scaling instead of the earlier approximately quadratic behavior, under different experimental conditions.

T1.justification: Proposition 1, its Appendix A induction proof, the objectives, and the gradient-estimator formulas remain mathematically unchanged after matching relocated equations. Expanded Kingman-process explanations and the explicit reference to the Leibniz integral rule explain existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: a differentiable variational family covering tree space, a closed-form density, no required MCMC subroutines, and competitive inference using fewer gradient evaluations. The added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 identifies underestimation for tree lengths of eight or greater and suggests a mismatch between approximately exponential long-branch posteriors and log-normal pairwise distributions. The computational discussion newly attributes observed near-linear VIPR scaling to likelihood evaluation and explains VBPI's scaling through SBN normalization and parameter growth. These materially extend the earlier limitations and mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds VIPR code and diagnostic-histogram access information, a more specific rooted-VBPI implementation reference, the MS simulation command, and runtime hardware details. It also explicitly discloses omission of VBPI's annealing schedule; v1 did not state this choice, so the disclosure alone does not establish a changed procedure.

R1.justification: The introduction adds ARTree and discussion of RAxML, neighbor-joining, and Phyloformer, distinguishing non-Bayesian reconstruction from marginal-likelihood estimation. Simulation references are also added. These broaden the context while retaining the original positioning against SBN-based inference and restricted matrix representations.

P1.justification: The six-section narrative remains recognizable. v2 copyedits prose, folds the notation subsection into Background, redistributes gradient explanations between Section 3.3 and Appendix C, reorganizes Appendix B into named subsections, and adds an Impact Statement.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout, redraws Figure 1, and merges the earlier DS1 and COVID figures into a six-panel Figure 2. It presents simplified benchmark tables in the main text and preserves complete versions in the appendix, while adding coverage, dataset-characteristic, parameter-count, and simulation displays and replacing the timing visualization.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical scrutiny through controlled scaling experiments, quantitative support-coverage checks, and known-tree diagnostics exposing a concrete approximation failure. These address important gaps in evaluating computational behavior and applicability, while preserving the original proof and benchmark results. Bootstrap and implementation disclosures improve auditability. Figure 6 retains an inconsistent COVID-19 caption despite describing simulated-data results, but this reporting flaw does not outweigh the validation gains.
